memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord replied to Moses, 'Whoever has sinned against me I will blot out of my book. Now go, lead the people to the place I spoke of, and my angel will go before you. However, when the time comes for me to punish, I will punish them for their sin.'" - Exod 32:33-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God does not accept Moses' offer. He cannot. One sinner cannot bear another sinner's guilt — the substitute must be spotless.

God's answer establishes something important: each person answers for their own sin. We cannot be saved by our parents' faith, our church membership, or someone else's godliness. The soul who sins is the one who dies (Ezek 18:20).

That is sobering. But look at what God says next: "Now go, lead the people." Judgement is real, and so is the continuing mission. God does not abandon the plan. His promise to bring them to the land stands, and His angel will go ahead of them. Grace does not cancel consequence, and consequence does not cancel grace.

The great question, then, is who can bear our sin if no fellow sinner can. Scripture answers with one name. Jesus, who knew no sin, was made sin for us (2 Cor 5:21). He alone qualified as the spotless substitute the law required (1 Pet 1:19).

So do not lean on someone else's faith. Come to Christ yourself. He is more than able.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your faith your own, or borrowed from someone else?
2. How do you hold together God's justice and His mercy?
3. What mission has God given you to keep walking in despite failure?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I come to You myself, in my own name and need, trusting Christ alone as my substitute. Amen.
